title: Beneath Thy Trees To-day We Met
description: Beneath Thy Trees To-day We Met in Tonic Solfa to ST ANNE, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: John Weiss wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 459, “For a Summer Festival”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST ANNE; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Be-neath Thy trees to day we met, A-mid Thy sum-mer flowers; And ev-ery heart is bless-ing yet These hap-py, fleet-ing hours.

lines: Beneath Thy trees to-day we met,
And every heart is blessing yet
But creeping shades to vespers call,
To make our latest shadows fall
Yes, even so; the summer leaf,
That Thou dost make them fair.
O, let us cherish nature's creed,
And live and bloom to Thee;
For only childlike hearts, we read,

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: John Weiss died in 1879.
credits: Words by John Weiss (1818–1879), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to ST ANNE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
